The test image shows a corn stalk split open, revealing shredded/fibrous pith with stringy vascular strands. The tissue looks gray/tan with what appear to be tiny dark specks. This is a **stem** disease.

Top candidates from KB descriptions:
- **Charcoal_Stalk_Rot**: "Shredded stalks with rotted pith leaving only stringy vascular strands, covered in tiny black spherical sclerotia" - very strong match
- **Diplodia_Stalk_Rot**: black structures in lower stalk rind
- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot**: black nodes, pith rot

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the strongest candidates.
Charcoal Stalk Rot reference shows shredded pith with dark areas. Similar shredding pattern. Let me check other candidates.
Diplodia shows stalk breakage but not the same shredded fibrous interior. Let me check more candidates.
Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dark spots on a green stalk, very different from the test image. Let me check other stem candidates.
Bacterial Stalk Rot shows external stalk browning, not the shredded fibrous interior. Let me check more candidates.
Anthracnose stalk rot shows shiny black lesions on the rind and reddish discoloration, different from the test image. Let me check Purple Leaf Sheath.
Purple Leaf Sheath shows dark lesions on green stalks, completely different. Let me check Diplodia Stalk Rot interior view.
Diplodia shows small black pycnidia on the rind surface, not the shredded fibrous interior. Now let me view a second Charcoal Stalk Rot reference to confirm the match.

This is a very strong match. This Charcoal Stalk Rot reference (Corn_Disease_32.jpg) shows the same shredded, fibrous stalk interior with stringy vascular strands and tiny dark sclerotia on a dark background, closely matching the test image.

The test image shows:
- Shredded pith with only vascular strands remaining
- Stringy, fibrous appearance
- Tiny dark specks (sclerotia) on the strands
- Gray/tan coloration giving a "charred" look

This perfectly matches the KB description: "Shredded stalks with rotted pith leaving only stringy vascular strands, covered in tiny black spherical sclerotia that give the internal stalk tissue a grey or charred appearance."

All 8 reference views used across 7 different classes (Charcoal_Stalk_Rot x2, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot x2, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose, Purple_Leaf_Sheath). Charcoal Stalk Rot is the clear winner.
